title: Where the Person Keeps the Last Word
subtitle: Design systems built for AI-assisted work, and design teams led and developed

bio.short: I'm a product and design leader who ships production code. At Bibel TV I built a design system that product managers and Claude build with directly. I also built a reply assistant where a person reads, edits and sends every letter. At Ninox I led five people across product design and UX writing, and I want to lead designers again while still designing.
bio.long:
Which work should AI take over, and where does a person keep the last word? I have answered that twice in work that is in use. As an independent consultant for Ninox in summer 2025, I designed an onboarding where AI builds a database from a plain-language description. The user edits the schema from the first step, with editor and chat side by side. Trial users write short prompts, so the first schema is rarely complete. The pattern became the basis for Ninox's public AI beta. At Bibel TV I built a reply assistant for viewer services that drafts in the support handbook's wording, formatting and standard phrases. A person reads every letter, edits the draft and decides every send.

Underneath that kind of work sits a design system AI tools can rely on. At Bibel TV I built the token architecture myself, in four tiers: primitives, semantic, component and page/view. It is served as an API and built to serve iOS, Android, web, connected TV and Figma from one source. Storybook is the source of truth, and Claude gets a closed list of valid token names. Checks refuse an off-system value and name the token to use instead. Product managers and Claude build with it directly.

At Ninox I sat on the Senior Leadership Team with five direct reports across product design and UX writing. I wrote the leveling framework for both disciplines and used it for growth plans and performance reviews. I hired two, promoted two, and owned the design system with joint governance with engineering. At Datameer I led a UX team from Berlin for five years, with part of the team in New York. I work closely with product and engineering on discovery, at the kickoff of larger initiatives and day to day in the sprint cycle.
